market_structure.regime: European Exchange Rate Mechanism fixed-band currency regime
market_structure.constraint: GBP had to remain inside its permitted ERM band versus the Deutsche mark.
market_structure.asymmetry: If the peg held, adverse movement was limited by the band; if the peg broke, sterling could devalue materially.

uk_conditions: UK housing and mortgage channel was highly sensitive to short rates because mortgages were generally floating rate.
Raising rates to defend sterling would quickly hit household cash flow and consumption.
germany_conditions: Bundesbank priority was monetary stability and anti-inflation credibility.
Bundesbank had limited willingness to cut rates to protect weaker ERM currencies.
macro_setup.political_constraint: UK authorities faced a choice between defending the ERM peg with recessionary rate hikes or allowing sterling to devalue.

trigger.event: Bundesbank President Helmut Schlesinger comments suggested broader currency realignment after lira adjustment.
trigger.interpretation: The Bundesbank was not willing to underwrite sterling at any price, making UK devaluation much more likely.

risk_reward.downside_if_wrong: Limited by the ERM band and ability to exit a liquid currency position; source case frames near-term loss as small relative to fund capital.
risk_reward.upside_if_right: Large devaluation gain if sterling exited or was forced out of the ERM.
risk_reward.probability_view: High probability over a short horizon once Schlesinger comments clarified German incentives.

liquidity_and_capacity.boe_reserves_constraint: The Bank of England and other central banks were the main remaining buyers; finite reserves constrained how much sterling could be bought to defend the peg.
liquidity_and_capacity.position_scale_note: Source case discusses Druckenmiller moving from a large existing short toward a much larger, highly concentrated position after the trigger.

trade_after_trade.primary_follow_on: Buy UK equities and government gilts after ERM exit because the UK would be free to cut rates. UK equities could also benefit from lower rates and weaker currency.
